# ProVoice study 1: natively set-valued labels (auto-generated by scripts/14_provoice.py)

## Data

1,446 answers from 12 drivers, 5 levels (LoA 0 = do nothing ... 4 = act autonomously). 93.2% of the answers are single levels, 98 are sets (97 contiguous, 1 with a gap). 45 features per answer: per-window summaries of the driver-state and vehicle frames (means, standard deviations, event fractions) and a one-hot code of the task asked about.

Accepted levels (an answer counts for every level in its set):

|       |   answers |
|:------|----------:|
| LoA 0 |       512 |
| LoA 1 |       319 |
| LoA 2 |       225 |
| LoA 3 |       178 |
| LoA 4 |       319 |

Answers per driver: 94-136 (median 121).

## Test performance (mean over 20 driver-level splits; lower is better except set accuracy)

## soft-CORN minus each other loss, paired over the 20 splits

Negative favours soft-CORN. Mean difference with the Nadeau-Bengio corrected resampled t-test (p) and its 95% interval; `seeds` is the number of splits (of 20) in which soft-CORN is better. The splits share drivers, so the correction matters: the 20 test sets of 3 drivers overlap heavily.
